Transfers performed by the tests (and money moved by defects) are reversed with compensating transfers; they remain visible in transaction history as tagged records.

requirements.text: A user should be able to enter a demo session, inspect their accounts and transaction history, transfer funds between their own accounts, and view basic profile information.
requirements.untestable_reason: Statement of purpose; verified indirectly through the concrete requirements below.

requirements.text: The application must never initiate real payments or connect to an external bank.
The target has one seeded demo customer.
The landing page provides a clearly labeled Enter Demo action.
It opens the demo dashboard without requiring a password or real identity information.
The header identifies the active demo customer and provides a Log out action.
Logging out returns the user to the landing page.
Protected dashboard views should not remain usable after logout; direct navigation to them should return the user to the landing page or an access-required state.
Refreshing while in a valid demo session should preserve that session.
A logged-out user must not regain access merely by refreshing a protected page.
The dashboard shows the customer's checking and savings accounts.
Each account displays a readable account name, a masked account identifier, account type, and current available balance in USD.
Balances are displayed to two decimal places.
The UI must not expose a full account identifier.
Selecting an account opens an account detail view with its current balance and related transaction history.
Account balances shown on the dashboard and detail view must agree with the latest successful transactions.
The user can transfer funds between the checking and savings accounts owned by the demo customer.
The transfer form includes source account, destination account, amount, and an optional memo.
The source and destination must be different accounts.
Same-account transfers must be rejected with a clear explanation and must not alter balances or create a transaction.
Amount must be a positive number greater than zero, with no more than two digits after the decimal point.
